I"m a huge fan of idle games and I've played tons of them. To this day I'm glad to say NGU Idle is one of the best.
NGU Idle features great challenges through an ever increasing number of features. Discovring those, making progress in them and finally completing them is a perpetual delight. You can't get bored in NGU Idle as there is always something new and fresh to do. Add to that a freaking TWO YEARS of real life pleasure to complete the beast and you know you have a winner.
Now, the game is not proof to a few cricisms. Offline mode is good but not perfect and I don't like the need to let the game run for hours if not days for something that don't require inputs. Depending of your playing habits it may be a deal breaker. Then the late game suffers from being obviously rushed by the developper : the last unlocked "feature" is annoying as hell and there is even signs of unfinished featu

eh its ok. very short game. watching the numbers go up is pretty fun tho

10/10 would waste 8000 hours again

It is an idle game that takes years. This makes the second year of game play a bit tedious but I enjoy the feeling of investment by putting off some additional growth for now for the massive exponential growth you'll achieve later.

 I also enjoy that the offline mode keeps making your stats better for up to a year after you last played which is ridiculous but feels secure.

Play this game if you want a good distraction for your spare moments for a couple years.

NGU Idle has one major flaw.

Acquiring and leveling up your armor and equipment is essential to progress in this game; while online, it occurs automatically, without human interference - as any idling game would allow. However, this cannot be acheived while offline, the game just doesn't allow it for an unknown reason. You have to keep the game running at all time.

This is where it falls short. There is absolutely no reason for such a design. 

Having to keep the game online at all times just doesn't cut it for me. It drains some mental space, which goes against the concept of an idle game - at least one that requires thousands of hours to reach completion.

All that being said. The rest is amazing. In that regard, if that's not a matter for you. You should play this game!

So, I really feel like any positivity towards this game is entirely comprised of either Nostalgia, or simple Stockholm Syndrome.

Doing anything in this game is an extreme grind. Basic automation features are locked behind somewhere between hundreds and thousands of hours of playtime, or a paywall (or a cheatwall). I thought Trimps was bad for having its automation a hundred hours in, but I'm pretty sure this is an order of magnitude above that.
It's a game targeted towards completionists who just want to see numbers *very slowly* reach 100, and... sure. You do you.

The entire thing is written in that awful 2000s-style lol-so-random meme internet humor where nothing can be serious, and nothing can be cohesive. You'll be fighting zombies, sentient cheese, the kitchen sink, and giant moles. Every line of story is a joke trying to one-up the last one with sheer nonsequiter. So unlike

Overall I don't recommend this game. This game is mostly a great game, but it's not a game for me. It may or may not be a great game for you.

I get anxiety from feeling like I'm missing out if I don't min-max my time optimally. I love how complex this game is, but I think about it too much while the game isn't actively running. This is probably an issue I have with the genre more than this game.
i got a big dopamine spike when i beat the last enemy in adventure mode, but the two years before that were boring.

A few good idea, and a humor that get stale quickly.
The game has a lot of content, that's for sure. (Even if about half of the 300 bosses in "normal" mode are a number with a "not done yet, sue me" kind of explanatory text.)

The grind, however, is ridiculous. "Challenges" basically require to reset your "number", which is your base progress (making it like you restarted). At least one of the challenge is horrible (Troll): you have to let the game run AND random annoying events will happen. e.g. You'll have to click on a button in a popup 30 times, and the buttons will randomly swap. You mis-click? Start again! I've ALT-F4 that crap and cancelled it.
But now, looking help online, I've learned I'll have to do ALL challenges, including this one.

♥♥♥♥ it.
